notes.text: The source begins J=Ob Pi-one and identifies morphisms in the groupoid with isomorphisms of two square-bracketed objects and then with isomorphisms of right pi-one torsors. It states that path composition is composition of the torsor hom maps. These are source statements, not independently proved claims in this reading pass. The extra groupoid suffix in the first Isom is unresolved.

The author says the groupoid has thus been reconstructed from tilde-X-prime(J) and its free right pi-one action, then asks how to reconstruct the G-prime action. The source question is Comment reconstituer l'opération de G-prime sur Pi-one ? The question mark above the lower diagram arrow is the author's own mark and is preserved separately from transcription uncertainty.

The page defines B-g as the inverse image of g, with pi-one- inserted before bitorseur. The source has image inv., not an expanded inverse. The two spots after B-g and the tip of the subsequent group connector remain visually doubtful; no expected mathematical construction was used to supply punctuation or a head.

The author next writes On note que l'on a and an asymmetrically enclosed parenthesis starting (grâce and ending with a square bracket. Inside it the argument is explicitly I in tilde-X-prime(I), although the adjacent formulas concern j and j-prime in J. I is retained rather than corrected; any expected J belongs to interpretation, not transcription. The final pair asserts identifications with contracted products by B-g.

The page carries 8 at the upper right and 15 at the bottom left. Both pencil marks are included without deciding their authorship or numbering system. The mathfrak X encoding follows the common notation convention and is not classified as a consequential mathematical correction.

Main adjudication accepts the candidate with localized doubts at the extra groupoid suffix, prose abbreviation point, cancellation, two low spots and connector tip. No date is written. Repeated X alphabets were checked as glyph encoding, not inferred changes of mathematical variable.
